It is completely understandable that you are feeling overwhelmed and missing her wisdom right now, especially when faced with such a surprising and delicate situation. It is natural to be deeply concerned about your grandchild's health and your daughter-in-law's choices. 

When you feel ready to talk to her, try to approach the conversation from a place of love and concern rather than judgment. You might gently acknowledge how miserable severe morning sickness can be, and encourage her to speak honestly with her OB/GYN. Doctors can offer safe, prescription alternatives to help manage nausea during pregnancy. By keeping the lines of communication open and focusing on her well-being and the baby's health, you can offer support while gently guiding her toward professional medical advice. Take your time to process your own shock and grief first, so you can have this conversation calmly when you are ready.
